title: skyBlip device status (v1)
description: The answer to {"command":"status"} on the config endpoint, and the one frame the device also sends without being asked: while a link is up, a change of flight state, a charging flip, a change of power level or a five-percent step of the state of charge pushes it to every subscribed central. One CBOR map in one notification, its keys numbered in link.v1.json; this schema describes it as a client decodes it, every key by its name and every enumeration by the names link.v1.json gives its codes. With every key at its widest it is 20 bytes, the payload every link guarantees, pinned byte for byte in firmware/test/products/test_comms_report.cpp. It carries what a pilot's screen shows and nothing a bench reads: why the device came up is 'reset' and whether a gauge is fitted is 'battery_valid' in diagnostics.v1, the address and the callsign are config.v1's. A key with no reading behind it is ABSENT, never a zero. Keys arrive in the order listed here, ascending by number, which scripts/check_status_schema.py holds the firmware and the registry to (firmware/core/comms/config_reports.cpp). The producer (firmware) owns this schema; consumers pin a version.

flight.description: The confirmed flight state. Every settings change and upload is refused unless this reads ground, so 'unknown' refuses too

upload.description: A firmware upload window is open: granted by the confirmation gesture on the device, true only on the ground, closed for good by a takeoff

battery_percent.description: State of charge, 0 where the device takes itself down rather than where a datasheet calls the cell empty, read on the discharge curve. ABSENT until the gauge has a reading of the cell, for ever on a board with no divider, and while the cable is in, because the divider reads the USB rail there and not the cell

charging.description: The cable is in. No pin says when the charge ends, so a full cell on the cable still reads true

power_level.description: What core/power's cutoff rule made of the same samples, three consecutive readings to step down and three to step back up. low is the cell past the knee, about 12%: the device asks for a charger and refuses nothing. critical, about 5%, refuses every durable write but the flight record. flat is the device taking itself down. unknown: no believable reading yet. The glass and the USB console print OK, LOW, CRITICAL, FLAT and --

went_dark_flat.description: The last time this unit went dark it was for a flat cell: the cutoff took it down, or a switch-on was refused below the boot lockout. The glass says FLAT BATTERY until a charger wakes the unit, and this outlives that frame: true for the whole of the one boot that followed, false from the boot after. The self-test page prints the same fact as WAS FLAT

die_temperature_c.description: Die temperature in whole degrees Celsius, rounded away from zero. ABSENT rather than zero when no reading younger than 30 seconds exists, because 0.0 C is a plausible hangar morning. Same key and same value as diagnostics.v1's.
